title: Restriction-choice dependence of quadratic APN extension
summary: Decide whether fixed-subspace extendability can depend on the admissible quadratic APN restriction, including whether pruning EA-equivalent representatives is sound.

formal_statement.body: In the source search framework, fix an admissible canonical linear-equivalence automorphism pair $(A,B)$ and fixed-space identifications. Can there be two admissible quadratic APN restrictions $G,G' :\operatorname{Fix}(A)\to\operatorname{Fix}(B)$ such that exactly one extends to a quadratic APN function $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ satisfying $F\circ A=B\circ F$? Exhibit such a tuple, or prove that extension existence is invariant under every admissible choice of $G$. In particular, settle whether pruning $G$ up to EA-equivalence preserves extendability.

scope.domain: Quadratic APN functions with prescribed linear self-equivalence
assumptions: (A,B) is admissible under the source canonical LE-automorphism framework
G maps Fix(A) to Fix(B) and is quadratic and APN
An extension F must be quadratic, APN, and satisfy F composed with A = B composed with F
scope.unresolved_remainder: No example with representative-dependent extension outcomes and no invariance theorem covering all admissible tuples was found.

progress.summary: The source notes that its search can fail for one restriction even if another restriction extends, and states that it is unknown whether this dependence can occur.
